title: Plan around long lead times and supply risk
summary: Some parts take months to arrive, and a single supplier can stop production. Find the risky parts early and plan around them.

beginner: Ask purchasing or your manufacturer for the lead time of every major part.
Mark the parts with the longest lead times and the ones with only one supplier.
Put the longest lead times into the roadmap as fixed dates.
Ask engineering whether a second, interchangeable part exists for the riskiest items.
Check lead times again every month, because they change.
intermediate: Score each part for lead time, single-source risk and end-of-life risk.
Order long-lead parts early where the risk justifies the cost.
Design in second sources for the highest-risk parts.
experienced: Set a supply-risk policy across products, including buffer stock.
Agree with finance how much to spend to reduce schedule risk.
Review end-of-life notices and plan redesigns before parts disappear.

canDelegateTo.task: Track lead times and order dates
Find second sources for risky parts

toolExamples.jira: Add each long-lead part as a dependency on the roadmap.
toolExamples.google-docs: Keep a risk score for each part in the BOM sheet.

definitionOfDone: Lead time known for every major part
pitfalls: Checking lead times once and never again
Relying on one supplier for a critical part
Ordering too late to save money
